gimbal_defaults.description: Inherited by every arm. An arm only states what makes it different.

arms.description: One entry per arm. Adding an arm needs no code changes.

layout.description: Descriptive only; real geometry comes from each arm's azimuth_deg.

nose_arm.description: Arm id the nose points along.

arm_length_m.description: Hub to centre, metres. Sets moment arms and the 3D model.

frame_class.description: Expected FRAME_CLASS on the flight controller. 4 is OCTAQUAD, which is what gives each arm a coaxial pair. This is the frame the motor function numbers were taken from, so the two must agree or the mixer addresses the wrong outputs. Changing it on the board needs a reboot, so the dashboard reports a mismatch rather than writing it.

frame_type.description: Expected FRAME_TYPE. 0 is PLUS, matching arms at 0/90/180/270.

battery.description: Reference only; live values come from telemetry.

axis.description: One gimbal axis: the servo driving it and the geometry of that drive.

channel.description: Output channel. 0 disables this axis: nothing is written to the flight controller and the pin is free for something else. 1-32 are SERVO1..SERVO32; above the controller's own output count means the CAN-to-PWM board, whose first output is channel 14.

sign.description: Direction. Absorbs how the servo and linkage are mounted. The only place direction is recorded: do not also set SERVOn_REVERSED.

us_per_deg.description: Pulse microseconds per servo degree. 11.11111 for a 500-2500 us, +/-90 degree servo.

servo_limit_deg.description: How far the servo itself may travel from centre. Describe the servo honestly; gimbal travel is bounded separately by tilt_limit_deg, which is enforced first.

min_us.description: Last-resort electrical clamp, not the operating limit.

trim_deg.description: Mechanical zero offset, servo degrees. On the inner axis this costs reachable tilt one degree for one degree, so centre the horn mechanically first.

gear_ratio.description: Servo degrees per gimbal degree. 2.0 for a 2:1 reduction. Use sign for direction, never a negative ratio.

tilt_limit_deg.description: Maximum geometric tilt per axis. The operating envelope, enforced before any other limit.

coupling.description: How much outer-axis motion leaks into the inner axis and must be added back to the inner command. 1.0 when the inner servo is mounted to the airframe, 0.0 when it rides on the outer ring.

channel.description: Output channel, 1-32 for SERVO1..SERVO32; 14 and up are the CAN-to-PWM node's outputs (14 is its first), driven as DroneCAN ESC commands. 0 does NOT free the pin: an unplaced mixer slot is placed by ArduPilot at boot, which puts MotorN on SERVO(N), turns that output into a DShot ESC pin, and takes its whole timer group into DShot with it. Give every motor an explicit channel on a group that carries only motors.

spin.description: The direction this propeller was OBSERVED to turn, seen from above the vehicle. Never written to the flight controller: editing this changes nothing on the drone. It records what the ESC actually does so the intended layout can be checked, and drives prop-fitting checks. To change a direction, edit `reversed` and reboot.

reversed.description: The only field that changes which way a propeller turns. Becomes a bit in SERVO_BLH_RVMASK, from which ArduPilot sends the DShot reverse command to that ESC. SERVO_BLH_RVMASK is @RebootRequired and the HAL only ORs into its reversed mask, so neither setting nor clearing this takes effect until the flight controller reboots. On a motor behind the CAN-to-PWM node the flight controller cannot apply this at all: it records the intent, and the direction has to be set in that ESC's own configuration or by swapping two motor wires.

test_sequence.description: The number MAV_CMD_DO_MOTOR_TEST expects. NOT the output channel: ArduPilot addresses motors by position in the frame's test order, which depends on FRAME_CLASS and FRAME_TYPE. null means not established, and the dashboard refuses to spin that motor.

function.description: The SERVOn_FUNCTION value that makes this channel a motor output: 33-40 for Motor1-Motor8. A Disabled output emits no signal at all, so a motor with no function set cannot spin. Which motor number an arm position maps to depends on FRAME_CLASS and FRAME_TYPE, so null means not established and the dashboard reports it rather than guessing.

id.description: Stable identifier used in commands and URLs. Must be unique.

status.description: live is wired and commandable, planned is described but not built, disabled is built but out of service. Only live arms are ever written to.

azimuth_deg.description: Where the arm physically points, from body +X toward body +Y. Sets the moment arm and tangential yaw direction.

mount_yaw_deg.description: How far the gimbal assembly is rotated about body Z. Sets how gimbal angles map to thrust direction. Usually equals azimuth_deg, but differs if a gimbal is bolted on rotated relative to its arm.

gimbal.description: Full gimbal override. Prefer the outer/inner shorthand for channel-only differences.

outer.description: Outer (roll) axis overrides. Mounted to the arm.

inner.description: Inner (pitch) axis overrides. Carried by the outer ring.

esc_telemetry_serials.description: SERIALn indexes that carry BLHeli T-wire telemetry. On the Matek H743-Wing, 4 is RX3 (USART3) and 6 is RX4 (UART4).

benchLimits.description: Hard bounds on what the dashboard will do, enforced server side.

command_rate_hz.description: Rate of the levelling loop and streamed aiming. Also drives the serial budget estimate.

benchController.description: Host-side levelling demo. NOT flight control; see Vector/docs/04-control.md.

level_gain.description: 0 leaves the gimbals with the airframe, 1 holds thrust at true world vertical.

lead_time_s.description: Seconds of attitude extrapolation, to offset servo lag. Measure it rather than guessing.

invert_roll.description: Bench sign flip. Once the right sign is known, fold it into the axis sign instead.
